cond_0001.intro: [Company name masked] is seeking a clinical veterinarian to help maintain the health, welfare, and regulatory responsibilities of the animals housed within our facility. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, provide clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Engage with the technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, direct and perform treatments and rechecks until resolution
Communicate with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plan and disposition
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, monitor and facilitate compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and study protocol development to ensure compliance with animal welfare, procedural and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission and review with the technical staff
Interact with operational teams to champion animal welfare, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals and coordinate scheduling of planned veterinary activities
Support management of the stock colony and oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing and facility sanitation programs
Participate in the creation, review, revision and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry and welfare
Research, develop and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend and holiday coverage
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Preferred Requirements
Attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.
cond_0001.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

cond_0036.intro: [Company name masked] is seeking a clinical veterinarian to help maintain the health, welfare, and regulatory responsibilities of the animals housed within our facility. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits.
cond_0036.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, coordinate clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Work with the Attending Veterinarian to perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments in coordination with the team
Engage with the technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, and coordinate treatments and rechecks until resolution
Share updates with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plans, and disposition
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), contributing to study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review, and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, help ensure compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines, and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description, and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and protocol development to support compliance with animal welfare, procedural, and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study-specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission, and share these with the technical staff
Coordinate with operational teams to support animal welfare, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals, and help schedule planned veterinary activities
Support management of the stock colony and contribute to oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing, and facility sanitation programs
Participate in the creation, review, revision, and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry, and welfare
Research, develop, and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction, and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits, and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend, and holiday coverage
cond_0036.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.

cond_0053.intro: [Company name masked] [Location masked] operational team is seeking a clinical veterinarian to maintain the health, welfare, and regulatory responsibilities of the animals housed within our facility. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] [Location masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits.
cond_0053.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, deliver clinical veterinary care for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Execute incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Lead regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Direct engagement with technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, and drive treatments and rechecks through to resolution
Communicate with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plan and disposition
Apply Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] [Location masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, ensure compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Own preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and protocol development to ensure compliance with animal welfare, procedural and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study-specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission and review with the technical staff
Champion animal welfare across operational teams, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals, and direct scheduling of planned veterinary activities
Oversee management of the stock colony and the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing and facility sanitation programs
Lead the creation, review, revision and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry and welfare
Research, develop and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend and holiday coverage
cond_0053.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license

Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits.
cond_0126.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, coordinate clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Work with the Attending Veterinarian to perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments in coordination with the team
Engage with the technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, and coordinate treatments and rechecks until resolution
Share updates with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plans, and disposition
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), contributing to study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review, and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, help ensure compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines, and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description, and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and protocol development to support compliance with animal welfare, procedural, and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study-specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission, and share these with the technical staff
Coordinate with operational teams to support animal welfare, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals, and help schedule planned veterinary activities
Support management of the stock colony and contribute to oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing, and facility sanitation programs
Participate in the creation, review, revision, and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry, and welfare
Research, develop, and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction, and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits, and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend, and holiday coverage
cond_0126.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.

cond_0162.intro: [Company name masked] is seeking a clinical veterinarian to help maintain the health, welfare, and regulatory responsibilities of the animals housed within our facility. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits.
cond_0162.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, coordinate clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Work with the Attending Veterinarian to perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments in coordination with the team
Engage with the technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, and coordinate treatments and rechecks until resolution
Share updates with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plans, and disposition
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), contributing to study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review, and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, help ensure compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines, and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description, and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and protocol development to support compliance with animal welfare, procedural, and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study-specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission, and share these with the technical staff
Coordinate with operational teams to support animal welfare, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals, and help schedule planned veterinary activities
Support management of the stock colony and contribute to oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing, and facility sanitation programs
Participate in the creation, review, revision, and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry, and welfare
Research, develop, and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction, and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits, and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend, and holiday coverage
cond_0162.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.

[Company name masked] [Location masked] operational team is seeking a clinical veterinarian to help maintain the health, welfare and regulatory responsibilities of the animals housed within our facility. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] [Location masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits.
cond_0210.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, provide clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Engage with the technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, direct and perform treatments and rechecks until resolution.
Communicate with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plan and disposition.
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records.
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] [Location masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, monitor and facilitate compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC).
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and study protocol development to ensure compliance with animal welfare, procedural and regulatory requirements.
Work with Study Directors to devise study specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission and review with the technical staff.
Interact with operational teams to champion animal welfare, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals and coordinate scheduling of planned veterinary activities.
Support management of the stock colony and oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing and facility sanitation programs.
Participate in the creation, review, revision and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry and welfare
Research, develop and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend and holiday coverage
cond_0210.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program, or equivalent practical experience where applicable
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Willingness to attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.

Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] [Location masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits.
cond_0336.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, provide clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Engage with the technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, direct and perform treatments and rechecks until resolution.
Communicate with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plan and disposition.
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records.
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] [Location masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, monitor and facilitate compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC).
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and study protocol development to ensure compliance with animal welfare, procedural and regulatory requirements.
Work with Study Directors to devise study specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission and review with the technical staff.
Interact with operational teams to champion animal welfare, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals and coordinate scheduling of planned veterinary activities.
Support management of the stock colony and oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing and facility sanitation programs.
Participate in the creation, review, revision and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry and welfare
Research, develop and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend and holiday coverage
cond_0336.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program, or equivalent practical experience where applicable
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Willingness to attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.
cond_0336.encouragement_text: Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.
cond_0336.values: We value excellence in execution and a clear focus on results. We aim to produce work that reflects high standards and a strong commitment to performance.

cond_0400.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Veterinarian to join our team at [Company name masked]. The role involves helping maintain the health, welfare, and regulatory responsibilities of the animals housed within our facility. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply. The [Company name masked] site is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the clinical and regulatory logic of laboratory animal medicine.
cond_0400.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, provide clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct regular vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Engage with the technical staff to monitor data reports, identify and address animals needing supportive care, respond to animal health concerns, direct and perform treatments and rechecks until resolution.
Communicate with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plan and disposition.
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records.
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, veterinary perspective, facility program review and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, monitor and facilitate compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines and standards that relate to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC).
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary expertise and consultation during study planning and study protocol development to ensure compliance with animal welfare, procedural and regulatory requirements.
Work with Study Directors to devise study specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission and review with the technical staff.
Interact with operational teams to champion animal welfare, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals and coordinate scheduling of planned veterinary activities.
Support management of the stock colony and oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing and facility sanitation programs.
Participate in the creation, review, revision and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry and welfare
Research, develop and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend and holiday coverage
cond_0400.requirements:

Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Preferred Requirements

This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.

cond_0439.intro: We are looking for a Clinical Veterinarian to join our team. [Company name masked] is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is useful, but not required — species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply.
cond_0439.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, provide clinical veterinary care for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Monitor data reports with technical staff to identify animals needing supportive care, direct and perform treatments and rechecks until resolution
Communicate with Study Directors regarding study animal issues, clinical evaluation findings, treatment plans and disposition
Document study data and facility records using Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, facility program review and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, monitor and support compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines and standards relating to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary input during study planning and protocol development to support compliance with animal welfare, procedural and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study-specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission, and review these with technical staff
Coordinate with operational teams on animal welfare matters, care and maintenance of laboratory animals, and scheduling of planned veterinary activities
Support management of the stock colony and oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing and facility sanitation programs
Participate in the creation, review, revision and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry and welfare
Research, develop and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend and holiday coverage
cond_0439.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Preferred Requirements
Continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
Advanced levels of education and/or years of experience (this position may be offered at different levels depending on qualifications)

[Company name masked] is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply.
cond_0466.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, provide clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Review data reports with technical staff to identify animals needing supportive care, address health concerns, and direct and perform treatments and rechecks until resolution
Document clinical evaluation findings, treatment plans, and disposition, and share updates with Study Directors regarding study animal issues
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, facility program review, and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, monitor and support compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines, and standards relating to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description, and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary input during study planning and protocol development to support compliance with animal welfare, procedural, and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study-specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission, and review these with technical staff
Coordinate with operational teams on animal welfare matters, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals, and schedule planned veterinary activities
Support management of the stock colony and oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing, and facility sanitation programs
Participate in the creation, review, revision, and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry, and welfare
Research, develop, and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction, and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits, and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend, and holiday coverage
cond_0466.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.

[Company name masked] is an AAALAC accredited contract research organization that conducts drug safety assessment studies for regulatory submission. In addition to general toxicology, our specialized focus includes developmental and reproductive studies in mostly rodents and rabbits. Prior experience in laboratory animal medicine is ideal, but not required as species-specific training and veterinary mentorship will be provided. Private practitioners looking for a career change are encouraged to apply.
cond_0502.responsibilities:
Key responsibilities will include but are not limited to:
Together with the Attending Veterinarian, provide clinical veterinary care and support for all animals in the facility (mostly rodents and rabbits)
Perform incoming health evaluations (acclimation release) and pre-screening activities for study animals such as physical and ocular examinations
Conduct vivarium rounds and animal welfare assessments
Review data reports with technical staff to identify animals needing supportive care, address health concerns, and direct and perform treatments and rechecks until resolution
Document clinical evaluation findings, treatment plans, and disposition, and share updates with Study Directors regarding study animal issues
Use Good Laboratory Practices (GLP) for documentation of study data and facility records
Serve as a voting member on the [Company name masked] Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC), including study protocol submission review, veterinary study updates at monthly meetings, policy and guideline review, facility program review, and inspections
Along with the Attending Veterinarian, monitor and support compliance with all applicable regulations, guidelines, and standards relating to animal care and use (e.g. USDA AWA, PHS, AAALAC)
Assist with the preparation of regulatory reports, AAALAC accreditation program description, and sponsor animal welfare evaluations
Provide veterinary input during study planning and protocol development to support compliance with animal welfare, procedural, and regulatory requirements
Work with Study Directors to devise study-specific veterinary palliative plans and humane endpoints for IACUC submission, and review these with technical staff
Coordinate with operational teams on animal welfare matters, advise on care and maintenance of laboratory animals, and schedule planned veterinary activities
Support management of the stock colony and oversight of the rodent sentinel health, preventative medicine, enrichment, social housing, and facility sanitation programs
Participate in the creation, review, revision, and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and policies relating to animal procedures, husbandry, and welfare
Research, develop, and assess potential new procedures and technologies appropriate to toxicology studies
Provide training, instruction, and guidance to scientific and operational staff as needed
May participate in sponsor conference calls, quality assurance audits, and regulatory inspections
Maintain records and inventory of controlled chemical substances in accordance with federal regulations
Rotating on-call schedule for after-hours/emergency, weekend, and holiday coverage
cond_0502.requirements:
Completion of an AVMA or EAEVE accredited Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM/VMD) program
Attainment of license to practice veterinary medicine in [Location masked] within one year of employment
Attend continuing education courses as appropriate to maintain state veterinary license
This position could be offered at different levels for candidates who qualify with a combination of advanced levels of education and/or years of experience.
cond_0502.inclusion: [Company name masked] is an equal opportunities employer committed to achieving 50/50 gender parity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. Women candidates are strongly encouraged to apply, and preference will be given to women in cases of equal qualification. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious beliefs, age, disability or other characteristics.
